verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.73
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 5.73

verses.pali: 8. Yodhājīvavagga
verses.english: 8. Warriors

verses.pali: Paṭhamadhammavihārīsutta
verses.english: One Who Lives by the Teaching (1st)

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “‘dhammavihārī, dhammavihārī’ti, bhante, vuccati.
verses.english: “Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

verses.pali: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hotī”ti?
verses.english: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”

verses.pali: “Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: “Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
verses.english: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

verses.pali: So tāya dhammapariyattiyā divasaṁ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
verses.english: They spend too much time studying that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu pariyattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
verses.english: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: So tāya dhammapaññattiyā divasaṁ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
verses.english: They spend too much time advocating that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu paññattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
verses.english: That mendicant is called one who advocates a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: So tena sajjhāyena divasaṁ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
verses.english: They spend too much time reciting that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu sajjhāyabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
verses.english: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: So tehi dhammavitakkehi divasaṁ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
verses.english: They spend too much time thinking about that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu vitakkabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
verses.english: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
verses.english: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

verses.pali: So tāya dhammapariyattiyā na divasaṁ atināmeti, nāpi riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
verses.english: They don’t spend too much time studying that teaching. They don’t neglect retreat, and they’re committed to internal serenity of heart.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Iti kho, bhikkhu, desito mayā pariyattibahulo, desito paññattibahulo, desito sajjhāyabahulo, desito vitakkabahulo, desito dhammavihārī.
verses.english: So, mendicant, I’ve taught you the one who studies a lot, the one who advocates a lot, the one who rehearses a lot, the one who thinks a lot, and the one who lives by the teaching.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhu, satthārā karaṇīyaṁ sāvakānaṁ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya, kataṁ vo taṁ mayā.
verses.english: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

verses.pali: Etāni, bhikkhu, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhu, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṁ vo amhākaṁ anusāsanī”ti.
verses.english: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
